comment: Credential provider profiles. Choosing an external provider turns OFF the engine's own save/fill prompts so only one manager offers to fill. Saved engine logins are never deleted. See docs/architecture/password-providers.md.

native_messaging.name: com.8bit.bitwarden
native_messaging.note: Only for desktop-app biometric unlock. Host name and allowed extension verified in bitwarden/clients apps/desktop/src/main/native-messaging.main.ts (commit 6d198af9512e, 2026-10-16); the desktop app writes ~/.mozilla/native-messaging-hosts/com.8bit.bitwarden.json.

native_messaging.name: com.1password.1password
native_messaging.note: Only for the desktop app's integration (unlock with the app, system authentication); the extension also works on its own with a sign-in in the browser. Host name and extension id as the desktop app writes them on Linux (~/.mozilla/native-messaging-hosts/com.1password.1password.json), from 1Password community reports and the extension's AMO id, read 2026-11-16, not yet measured with the app installed. For a browser 1Password does not know, its binary name must be in /etc/1password/custom_allowed_browsers (support.1password.com/additional-browsers): nulavio-doctor (a package install; nulavio doctor in a source checkout) says so; Nulavio never writes that file.
